propositions: Every synchronous MCP tool body runs directly on the uvicorn event loop coroutine, not on a worker thread, causing the loop to block for the entire duration of slow tool calls and starving concurrent requests including initialize handshakes.

During a long tool call (15-20 minute review_plan, 9-11 minute completion-verifier, or 177-second list_tickets), the server stops responding to all requests—initialize, tools/list, health checks—until the tool returns, manifesting as backlog draining in milliseconds once the loop is released.

The first client to initialize after a redeploy fails with 30+ second timeouts because all agents reconnect simultaneously and the first one to arrive hits a long-running tool call; subsequent clients connect instantly after the backlog drains.

The fix wraps synchronous tool bodies with anyio.to_thread.run_sync to run them on worker threads off the event loop, preserving contextvars for op-cert signing and keeping the certified-tools gauge instrumentation working correctly.

Cold-start work, store size, boto3 imports, static-token auth, and provisioning contention are exonerated by measurement: cold authenticated initialize at cutover fires in 30ms against a 2.2GB store; the process starvation is purely from event-loop-blocking tool bodies, not from external I/O or initialization.
The design follows the precedent established by ticket c2ba (melting-resting-serpent) which moved emit_code_review_artifact off the loop using asyncio.to_thread for the sibling review-bot service.
